reference: No GNU CLI is a one-to-one oracle for this Bash loadable's login/logout/boot/shutdown/btmp API. Runnable cases are documented-contract checks: Bash type/help metadata plus fixed-width Linux utmp records emitted by an independent Bash encoder at the glibc 384-byte record layout. Writer cases verify documented fields through readback and independent Python struct decoding of record types, sizes and representative fields. Host-default accounting paths are deferred. Writer record types and sizes are also decoded independently with Python struct for the Linux/glibc little-endian 384-byte layout.
coverage: Bash builtin availability metadata and help text for documented subcommands
dump formatting and USER_PROCESS filtering from independently encoded records
btmp latest-N selection and recovery of complete records before a torn tail
btmp record creation through an explicit relative path and readback
login/logout lifecycle through explicit relative utmp, wtmp, and lastlog paths
boot and shutdown wtmp records through an explicit relative path
lastlog dump formatting for the fixture login record
exclusions: No matching GNU command exposes the same subcommand API, so these are contract cases rather than fabricated parity comparisons.
Default /var/run and /var/log accounting paths are not touched; disposable-VM integration is deferred.
Cross-checking records with system who/last/lastlog consumers is outside this loadable-only suite.
Binary layout checks target the pinned Linux/glibc little-endian ABI; they do not claim cross-platform utmp layout portability.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports utmp as an enabled loadable builtin without invoking an accounting operation.
Check the documented help exposes the login/logout, wtmp, dump, lastlog, and btmp forms advertised by utmp_doc.
cases.script:
doc=$(help utmp)
[[ $doc == *"utmp login"* && $doc == *"utmp logout"* && $doc == *"utmp boot"* && $doc == *"utmp shutdown"* && $doc == *"utmp dump"* && $doc == *"utmp lastlog dump"* && $doc == *"utmp btmp read"* ]]
printf 'documented-subcommands-present\n'

cases.purpose: Verify an unrecognized verb fails with a diagnostic while leaving the fixture clean.
Read independently encoded 384-byte Linux utmp records, format the USER_PROCESS entry, and omit a LOGIN_PROCESS entry.
Check btmp read selects the newest requested whole record and reports a one-byte torn tail while still displaying that record.
Exercise the documented btmp record form using a relative fixture path, then check its user, line, host, and timestamp through btmp read.
cases.script:
utmp btmp record -f failures alice pts/8 edge-host
[[ -s failures ]]
row=$(utmp btmp read -f failures -n 1)
[[ -n $row && $row != *$'\n'* && $row == *alice*pts/8*edge-host* ]]
[[ $row =~ [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\ [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$ ]]
printf 'relative-btmp-record-roundtrip\n'
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYRECORDS'
import struct
from pathlib import Path
raw=Path('failures').read_bytes()
assert len(raw)==384*1
assert [struct.unpack_from('<h',raw,p)[0] for p in range(0,len(raw),384)]==[7]
assert raw[8:40].split(b'\0')[0]==b'pts/8'
assert raw[44:76].split(b'\0')[0]==b'alice'
assert raw[76:332].split(b'\0')[0]==b'edge-host'
assert Path('failures').stat().st_mode & 0o777==0o600
print('independent record types verified')
PYRECORDS

cases.purpose: Check login creates an active fixture record and logout clears it and appends a dead marker to the fixture wtmp, using only relative paths.
cases.script:
utmp login -u active.utmp -w history.wtmp -l lastlog.fixture runner pts/demo host-a
[[ -s active.utmp && -s history.wtmp ]]
live=$(utmp dump active.utmp)
[[ -n $live && $live != *$'\n'* && $live == *runner*pts/demo*host-a*pid=* ]]
lastlog=$(utmp lastlog dump lastlog.fixture)
[[ $lastlog == uid=*' line=pts/demo host=host-a time='* && $lastlog != *$'\n'* ]]
[[ $lastlog =~ time=[0-9]+$ ]]
utmp logout -u active.utmp -w history.wtmp pts/demo
[[ -z $(utmp dump active.utmp) ]]
history=$(utmp dump history.wtmp)
[[ -n $history && $history != *$'\n'* && $history == *runner*pts/demo*host-a* ]]
tail=$(utmp btmp read -f history.wtmp -n 1)
[[ -n $tail && $tail != *$'\n'* && $tail == *pts/demo* && $tail != *runner* && $tail != *host-a* ]]
printf 'private-login-logout-transition\n'
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYRECORDS'
import struct
from pathlib import Path
raw=Path('active.utmp').read_bytes()
assert len(raw)==384*1
assert [struct.unpack_from('<h',raw,p)[0] for p in range(0,len(raw),384)]==[8]
raw=Path('history.wtmp').read_bytes()
assert len(raw)==384*2
assert [struct.unpack_from('<h',raw,p)[0] for p in range(0,len(raw),384)]==[7, 8]
print('independent record types verified')
PYRECORDS

cases.purpose: Verify the documented boot and shutdown entries append to an explicit relative wtmp and are readable as the expected reboot/shutdown records.
cases.script:
utmp boot lifecycle.wtmp
utmp shutdown lifecycle.wtmp
[[ -s lifecycle.wtmp ]]
rows=$(utmp btmp read -f lifecycle.wtmp)
[[ $rows == *reboot*~*shutdown*~* && $rows == *$'\n'* ]]
printf 'boot-and-shutdown-appended\n'
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PYRECORDS'
import struct
from pathlib import Path
raw=Path('lifecycle.wtmp').read_bytes()
assert len(raw)==384*2
assert [struct.unpack_from('<h',raw,p)[0] for p in range(0,len(raw),384)]==[2, 1]
print('independent record types verified')
PYRECORDS

cases.purpose: Exercise login/logout and boot/shutdown against the loadable's default accounting locations and validate effects on the operating-system session databases.
cases.reason: Default-path integration never executed; the candidate hard-codes absolute paths, but a private user+mount namespace can substitute driver/fixture-owned files without touching the VM's real accounting databases.
